notes:
Status: closed-lost — customer elected to self-host. Short bullets from AE notes:
- 2025-09 discovery: heavy emphasis on control + cost; infra lead explicitly said 'we can't rely on multi-tenant pricing long-term'.
- Ran 6-week PoC (Dec-Jan) vs Redwood hosted API + 1:1 cost model; infra reported ~55-65% token cost reduction once quantized + Triton/TensorRT inference path matched perf targets.
- Security team blocked hosted: needed HSM/KMS integration, SAML + org-wide audit retention policy, and strict data residency. They required proof of SOC2 + on-prem deployment feasibility; procurement said on-prem mandatory for some data classes.
- SE (Priya) supported architecture workshop; recommended Dedicated and Private options but Meridian infra favored vLLM + TGI + TensorRT + internal ops.
- Last engagement: 2026-02-20 call with CIO — they confirmed decision to build in-house; cited budgeting constraints and desire to own model lifecycle.
- Quote from CTO: 'We value Redwood's docs and speed, but we need absolute control over inference stack and unit economics.'
- AE attempted winback: offered pricing credits for Dedicated and a 6-month pilot; no response after procurement freeze.
- Internal note: good technical fit for Dedicated/private, but loss driven by organizational policy + cost math.
- Suggested follow-ups: share self-host best practices doc, track production infra pain points, offer migration path to Redwood Private if policy relaxes.

reason_lost: Customer prioritized control and lower long-term unit cost; chose vLLM/TGI/TensorRT self-host stack. Security and procurement requirements (on-prem KMS, audit retention, data residency) made hosted options non-starter.
sales_play_notes: Win/loss summary: technical fit OK, commercial tension around committed spend vs capex. No single exec champion after Q4 re-org. Recommend 6-12 month nurture cadence: share migration templates, TCO comparisons, and targeted case studies showing hybrid migrations.
